title: Consumers: groups, positions, stored offsets, and commits
outcome: Predict replay from the committed next offset and avoid acknowledging unfinished work.
useCase: A reporting group with controlled replay.
drawbacks: Incorrect offset handling can lose or duplicate business work.
version: Kafka 4.1 KRaft · lab Ruby 3.3 / Rails 7.2 · legacy Rails adaptation notes
cue: Fetch is not finish. Commit only completed progress.

trace.title: Partition assignment
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

A consumer group shares partition responsibility among its members. A different group has independent progress and can read the same retained records.

Within a group, one assigned member normally owns a partition at a time under the selected group protocol.

Distinguish fetched position, a client’s stored progress, and committed group offsets. Exact APIs vary by library.

A committed offset conventionally identifies the next record to resume from, not the last business event ID.

Process the durable effect before committing the relevant completed progress. A crash after effect but before commit replays it.

Committing too early can skip unfinished work after a crash. Auto offset reset applies when there is no usable committed position; earliest does not rewind a healthy group on every restart.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Assigned partition → fetch → validate → DB transaction → commit completed progress.

Parallel processing needs a contiguous completion frontier: do not commit past an earlier unfinished record merely because a later one finished.

Test a consumer restart with an existing group and then a new group. Explain the difference from resetting offsets deliberately.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail:
A high fetched position does not mean business work completed. More group members than partitions can leave members idle.

An automatic progress setting can acknowledge work before your code intended.
